item.title: Ebonyi pensioners endorse Nwifuru for second term
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) has endorsed Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, for a second term in office ahead of the 2027 governorship election, citing his administration’s payment of outstanding pension and gratuity arrears dating back to 1996. The union also conferred an award on Nwifuru as the most pensioner-friendly governor in recognition of what it described as his commitment to the welfare of retired workers in the state. The endorsement was announced during the presentation of the award to the governor in Ebonyi State. The National President of NUP, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, represented by his deputy, Abdulahi Onuh, commended Nwifuru for clearing the backlog of pensions and gratuities owed to retired workers from 1996. Onuh described the achievement as significant, saying the governor had distinguished himself through his administration’s intervention in the welfare of pensioners. He said, “Clearing pensions and gratuity of pensioners from 1996 till date is not a small number of years. The Governor has written his name in gold. “While in Kano, I thought that the Governor of Kano State is number one. I never knew that coming to Ebonyi State, the Kano Governor will be number two. “To clear a backlog of pensions and gratuity from 1996 till date is a very big achievement. May God elongate the life of Ebonyi Governor. The Governor has done a lot.” He also commended the state government over plans to extend the state health insurance scheme to retirees, describing the initiative as another important intervention in their welfare. The NUP national leadership, however, urged the state government to implement pension increases and harmonisation of benefits, noting that pension increments were provided for under the Constitution. Onuh called on pensioners to reciprocate the governor’s gesture by voting for him in the 2027 election. He said, “You are indebted to the Governor. Use your PVCs and show him appreciation by voting for him in the 2027 general election. “When you go home, off your clothes and tell your children that as of two years back, they were taking you to the hospital every week. You were calling your children both home and abroad, bring me my medical allowance. “But the Governor has reduced the strength of your children in Nigeria and outside. Go and pay him back. Tell your children, tell your in-laws to pay the Governor back by voting for him.” Also speaking, the Ebonyi State Chairman of NUP, Comrade Anna Ibiam, said retired workers had endured years of unpaid pensions and gratuities before Nwifuru assumed office. She said some pensioners died while waiting for their entitlements, adding that the governor’s administration had changed the situation through regular pension payments and the clearance of outstanding gratuities. “Many of our colleagues died waiting without receiving their gratuity. item.title: Reps threaten action against Science Minister over bill
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has threatened legislative action against the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, over his failure to attend a public hearing on a bill seeking to establish a National Research and Innovation Development Fund. The lawmakers warned that the ministry’s absence could delay the proposed legislation and undermine President Bola Tinubu’s efforts to attract international research grants and funding from development partners, donor agencies, United Nations organisations and Nigerians in the diaspora. The House Committee on Science and Technology expressed displeasure that neither the minister nor the ministry’s Permanent Secretary or any senior representative attended the hearing, despite the ministry’s direct responsibility for the subject matter of the bill, HB 2821. The committee also noted that the proposed legislation was sponsored by the executive and transmitted to the National Assembly by President Tinubu. Speaking at the hearing, a member of the committee, Hon. Ahmed Usman Jaha, representing Chibok, Damboa and Gwoza Federal Constituency of Borno State, described the ministry’s absence as a possible act of sabotage against the working relationship between the executive and legislative arms of government. Jaha, who spoke on behalf of the committee, said it was difficult to understand why a ministry directly concerned with an executive-sponsored bill of national importance would fail to participate in its consideration. “Unfortunately, some members of the executive are by extension sabotaging this relationship. The reason why I call it sabotage is that I see no reason whereby the executive can present a bill to the House for consideration, and that bill has national importance, but the ministry responsible for it will not show up,” he said. He disclosed that the committee had invited the Ministers of Justice, Innovation, Science and Technology, Education, Environment, Agriculture and Food Security, Health, Livestock Development, and Industry, Trade and Investment, alongside other stakeholders, to contribute to the legislative process. However, none of the invited ministers attended the hearing. Jaha said the absence of the Science and Technology Minister was particularly concerning, insisting that either the minister or the Permanent Secretary should have appeared before the committee. “We are not averse to the Ministry of Justice and other ministries that are not directly linked to the bill. But our concern this time around is the Ministry of Science and Technology. If any minister may not have time to attend, they may end up sending representatives. But the Minister of Science and Technology himself, who is more or less the sponsor of the bill, or in a worst-case scenario, the Permanent Secretary, must show up,” he said. item.title: Singer Boj shares essential items to survive Detty December in Lagos
item.description: Nigerian singer and songwriter BOJ has shared some of his essential items for navigating the Detty December festivities, advising partygoers to prepare for the heat, crowded venues and messy environments expected during the festive season. Speaking in an interview with LSTV, the singer said the December festivities would be particularly intense, urging people to come prepared. We linked up with Nigerian singer, songwriter, and creative director Boj [ @BojDRB ] for his Detty December ESSENTIALS and he spoke facts . pic.twitter.com/tskJV12t3C — LSTVWW (@lstvww) November 12, 2026 “Everywhere is going to be hot. I don’t know if you guys have of El Nino,” he said. Listing his must-have items, BOJ identified a face towel as one of the most important things to carry, noting that the heat and activities during the festive period would make it particularly useful. “First of all, you’re going to need a face towel, very key,” he said. He also recommended wearing shoes other than white, warning that partygoers would likely encounter spilled drinks, water and crowded environments at various events. “Personally, I also think that shoes that are not white because you’re going to be stepping everywhere, you’re going to be choked of water. Just always have that because it’s going to be a lot of drinking,” he added. Detty December has become a major feature of Nigeria’s end-of-year entertainment calendar, attracting Nigerians in the diaspora and international visitors for a series of concerts, parties, festivals and social events. item.title: Zamfara commissioner dies at 50, governor mourns
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has mourned the death of the state’s Commissioner for Commerce, Tasiu Musa Shinkafi, who died on Wednesday at the age of 50. Shinkafi reportedly died in a hospital in Kaduna following a brief illness. In a condolence message, Lawal described his death as an irreparable loss to the state government, his family and the people of Zamfara. The governor said, “With heavy hearts and in total submission to the will of Almighty Allah (T), we received the shocking news of the passing of the Commissioner for Commerce, Tasiu Musa Shinkafi. “Tasiu’s death is a great loss not only to his family and the state government, but also to the people of Zamfara. “He will be remembered for his dedication, honesty, and commitment to Zamfara State.” Lawal recalled that Shinkafi had previously served as Commissioner for Youth and Sport before his redeployment to the Ministry of Commerce. Describing the deceased as a valued member of his administration and a brother in service, the governor said his contributions to governance, politics and public service would be remembered. He prayed to Almighty Allah to forgive the deceased’s shortcomings and grant his family the strength to bear the loss. item.title: Oyo SDP candidate sues INEC over omission from list
item.description: By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Oyo State, Olusegun Agboola, has dragged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) before the Federal High Court in Abuja over the omission of his name from the commission’s list of candidates for the 2027 governorship election. Agboola alleged that unnamed political interests were behind his exclusion, describing the development as illegal, inexplicable and politically motivated. The SDP candidate, who maintained that he had fulfilled all the necessary electoral requirements, said he was seeking a court order compelling INEC to include his name on the list. In a statement on Thursday, Agboola expressed concern over what he described as the selective omission of his name despite his qualification to contest the election. He said, “The illegal and unexplainable omission of my name from the latest INEC published list as the SDP governorship candidate for Oyo State is perplexing. “Of all qualified candidates, my name was singled out and omitted from the published list without any reason from INEC.” Agboola alleged that the omission was an attempt to weaken the SDP’s political standing ahead of the election, claiming that some politicians in rival parties were uncomfortable with the party’s agenda and positions on issues affecting the state. He said, “I have been told that some people from other popular parties are behind it. They are not comfortable with all we stand for, so they want to use INEC to diminish our campaign and suppress all our efforts.” Expressing confidence in the judicial process, the candidate said he expected the court to compel INEC to correct the omission, questioning why he had to seek legal intervention after complying with the prescribed procedures. “We have followed due process and the court will soon mandate INEC to include our names, but why is that necessary?” he queried. He further alleged that his exclusion was part of a broader attempt by unnamed political interests to manipulate the electoral process and influence the outcome of the 2027 governorship election. “Some people want to use every means possible to doctor the outcome. This is sad for our democracy and shows the integrity of the umpire is damaged if this anomaly is not loudly corrected with a very public announcement from the INEC chairman,” he added. Agboola said Oyo State needed practical and sustainable solutions to unemployment, insecurity, inadequate infrastructure and other socio-economic challenges. He argued that addressing the problems required deliberate, systemic and long-term interventions rather than temporary measures. item.title: Armed robbers steal goods worth 1mn euros in Paris jewellery heist
item.description: Armed robbers stole goods worth more than one million euros ($1.1 million) from a De Beers jewellery store in Paris Thursday before fleeing on scooters, authorities and a police source told AFP. The suspects, carrying long guns, targeted the store in the city’s 2nd arrondissement at around 11:00 am (1000 GMT). During the robbery, they brandished their weapons but did not open fire, and no one was injured, according to the Paris police. A police source estimated the value at more than one million euros, confirming an earlier report by French broadcaster Europe 1. Four suspects in balaclavas, one armed with an assault rifle, are believed to have fled on motorbikes towards the motorway, according to the same source, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The Paris police said it has deployed significant resources to track down the perpetrators. The organised crime unit has opened an investigation into “armed robbery by an organised gang”, the prosecutor’s office said. Industry giant De Beers has long dominated the trade in diamonds from southern Africa. The post Armed robbers steal goods worth 1mn euros in Paris jewellery heist appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Politicians deceive voters to win elections – Kukah
item.description: The Catholic Bishop of Sokoto Diocese, Matthew Kukah, has accused politicians of making unrealistic promises during election campaigns to secure votes, rather than preparing Nigerians for the realities and challenges of governance. Kukah said politicians often deploy attractive images, grand promises and appealing narratives to sell voters a vision of a better society, only to abandon their commitments after assuming office and begin offering excuses for their inability to deliver. He spoke on Thursday in Abuja at a public symposium organised by the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies (NILDS) in collaboration with The Kukah Centre. To illustrate the disconnect between campaign promises and governance, Kukah narrated the story of a politician who used impressive images of tarred roads, bridges, beautiful houses and children in smart school uniforms to persuade voters during his campaign. According to him, the politician won the election, but three years later, residents complained that none of the promised projects had been executed. When confronted, the politician reportedly told them: “You are confusing campaign with governance. What I did was purely a simple campaign. Governance is a difficult part.” Kukah said the response reflected a recurring pattern in Nigeria’s political system, where politicians make ambitious promises to win elections but resort to excuses after taking office. He said, “And this is why we have Nigerian politicians turn around, once they have been sworn in and after telling us all the things they want to do, and say, ‘We didn’t know that the treasury was so empty.’ Then, they start giving one excuse after the other.” The bishop argued that politicians were often more interested in creating attractive campaign narratives than communicating the realities of governance. He, however, said voters had a responsibility to interrogate political promises and assess their feasibility rather than accept campaign messages at face value. He stated, “The point I am making is that it is the business of politicians to seduce, deceive or tell us things we can’t do just to win our votes. But we are sufficiently knowledgeable, and our experience should help us to test the limits of the claims that politicians make.” Kukah urged Nigerians to develop the capacity to question politicians, scrutinise their proposals and demand accountability, stressing that citizens should not wait until elections are over before engaging the political elite. He also called for political choices that transcend ethnic, religious and class considerations. item.title: FG concessions Port Harcourt airport for 30 years, eyes two others
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has signed a 30-year concession agreement for the Port Harcourt International Airport as part of efforts to attract private investment, improve operational efficiency and unlock the economic potential of the nation’s loss-making airports. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja during the signing of the concession agreement with Port Harcourt Airport Company Limited. Keyamo said the concession was aimed at improving the operational efficiency of the airport, boosting revenue generation and unlocking its commercial potential. He explained that the Federal Government had been using profits generated from major airports to subsidise the operations of other airports that were running at a loss. According to him, the cost of maintaining airports, including personnel expenses, diesel and other operational requirements, has continued to put pressure on government finances. The minister said government lacked the resources to fully develop the non-aeronautical components of some airports, making private sector participation necessary. “Some of our airports are being run at a loss. We make so much money from some of our primary airports, and most of those profits are ploughed into running other airports,” Keyamo said. He noted that the concession had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council, adding that the process was not a sudden decision but one that successive administrations had struggled to implement. Keyamo said previous attempts to concession airports were frustrated by resistance from labour unions and court cases involving the government. He, however, attributed the successful conclusion of the process to negotiations with aviation unions, saying the government had secured their agreement before signing the deal. The minister assured workers that the concession would not lead to job losses or a reduction in their conditions of service. He said Tinubu had directed that the welfare of aviation workers must be protected throughout the concession process. “President Bola Tinubu was very concerned about that, that no worker should lose his job. The conditions of service should remain the same,” he said. Keyamo added that the concessionaire would be subjected to performance reviews every five years to ensure compliance with the terms of the agreement. He warned that the government could take back the airport if the concessionaire failed to meet the agreed standards. The minister also disclosed that the government had received proposals from investors interested in developing other airports, including those in Benin and Yola. He said the government was considering the proposals as part of efforts to make more airports commercially viable. item.title: Tinubu: Wike inaugurates Rivers campaign council, directs it to recruit 5 new voters daily
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has inaugurated the Presidential Campaign Council for Rivers State and directed its members to recruit at least five new voters daily to deliver votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election. Wike, who performed the inauguration on Thursday, set a target of three million votes for the president in the state. He called for hard work, focus and issue-based campaigning, and dismissed recent confusion over appointments into the committees. “I am sure by Monday the list of the chairmen and members of the various sub-committees will have been prepared so that the chairmen can kick-start by inviting their various committee members. It is very important,” he said. The minister said victory in Rivers was not in doubt. “Everybody knows that we are going to win election in Rivers State. So we are not talking about winning now,” he said. Wike recalled how the three million figure came up in a discussion with Senate President Godswill Akpabio. “He said, ‘How much is the registered votes here?’ I said, ‘over three million.’ He said, ‘Okay, you will bring three million.’ I said, ‘Well, we will try’. I know that three million, if we work hard, it ia easy.” Wike urged members of the council to treat their appointments as an opportunity to work for the Rainbow Coalition, and called on them to stay united and disciplined in the face of provocation from the opposition. He cited the Olubadan and former governor of Oyo State, Oba Rasheed Ladoja who he said spoke a day earlier when the National Working Committee of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) paid him a courtesy visit in Oyo State. “He said if he was still in politics, if he was not a traditional ruler today, he would have joined Rainbow Coalition, that is the best way to bring every shade of opinion, members of other political parties to join hands to make sure that Mr. President is re-elected come 2027,” Wike said. Governor Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers State described the new council as bigger, wider and better coordinated than the structure that delivered victory for the president in 2023. He said former political adversaries had now closed ranks to work together for the state and the president. “Nothing is impossible. The only thing that is not possible is to revive the dead. If we take this as a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisively with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023,” Fubara said. The governor assured members who were left out that they would be accommodated in the subcommittees. He also warned against double-dealing and urged members to work with sincerity rather than profess loyalty in public while sabotaging the effort behind closed doors. “I am here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day, in private and in secret: I have taken this position,” Fubara said. item.title: Imo East: Court orders INEC to recognise Nwole as NDC candidate
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately recognise and publish the name of Uche Nwole as the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the Imo East senatorial election scheduled for January 16, 2027. In a judgment delivered by Justice Mohammed Umar, the court said it was satisfied that the plaintiff, Nwole, was the bona fide winner of a primary election conducted by the party, which it noted was duly monitored by INEC. It held that, in view of Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act 2026, the NDC ought to have nominated and forwarded the plaintiff’s name to the electoral body as its senatorial candidate. According to the court, the NDC could not lawfully nominate a consensus candidate other than the one who emerged from its INEC-monitored primary election. Consequently, aside from issuing an order of perpetual injunction restraining the party from nominating or submitting any other name for the election, the court barred INEC from accepting, listing or publishing any purported NDC candidate who allegedly emerged from a primary election that was never held or monitored by the commission, or any purported consensus candidate whose nomination breached Sections 87(1) and (3) of the Electoral Act 2026. The judgment followed suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/1225/2026, in which the NDC, INEC and Hon. Onyeagucha Uchechukwu were the 1st to 3rd defendants. The plaintiff alleged that although he secured the highest number of valid votes cast in the primary election, the party sidelined him and chose the 3rd defendant as its flag bearer for the senatorial poll. Justice Umar said that, after careful examination of all the evidence adduced in the matter, he was satisfied that the plaintiff’s case deserved to succeed. He therefore granted all seven principal reliefs the plaintiff sought. Among other things, the court held: “A declaration is made that, upon the construction of the clear, unambiguous and express provisions, spirit and tenor of Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act 2026, the 1st Defendant duly conducted primary elections, which were duly monitored by the 2nd Defendant, for all aspirants seeking to be nominated as the candidate of the party to contest the elective position of Senator representing Imo East Senatorial District in the 2027 general election. “A declaration is made that, upon a careful construction and interpretation of Section 87(1), (2) and (3) of the Electoral Act 2026, the 1st Defendant, having conducted a primary election in accordance with Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act, cannot lawfully nominate a consensus candidate to contest the office of Senator representing Imo East Senatorial District in the 2027 general election. “A declaration is made that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), being a body established by law, must at all times obey its constitution; respect, observe and implem

item.title: Nigeria’s exports to China rise 81% to $2.25bn
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Nigeria’s exports to China rose by 81 per cent to $2.25 billion in the first half of 2026, while bilateral trade between both countries increased by 35 per cent to $17.4 billion, the Chinese Embassy has said. The Cultural Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria and Director of the China Cultural Centre in Nigeria, Mr Yang Jiaxing, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at the 2026 launch ceremony of the Voice of Nigeria (VON) China-Nigeria Bridge Programme. Yang attributed the growth to expanding economic cooperation between the two countries, saying China’s zero-tariff policy for 53 African countries, including Nigeria, which took effect in May 2026, would create more opportunities for Nigerian exports. He said China’s trade with African countries reached $207.4 billion in the first half of 2026, while imports from the continent rose to $28.5 billion between May and June. According to him, imports from Nigeria recorded year-on-year growth of more than 40 per cent in both May and June, reflecting stronger trade relations between the two countries. He said: “In the first half of this year, bilateral trade between China and Nigeria reached $17.4 billion, up 35 per cent year-on-year. China’s imports from Nigeria amounted to $2.25 billion, representing a remarkable increase of 81 per cent.” Yang described the China-Nigeria Bridge Programme as a platform for promoting cultural understanding, media cooperation and closer relations between citizens of both countries. The programme, jointly initiated by the Chinese Embassy, the Africa Regional Bureau of Xinhua News Agency and VON, provides Mandarin lessons and reports on China-Africa relations. Also speaking, the Director-General of VON, Jibrin Baba Ndace, said the introduction of Mandarin as the organisation’s ninth broadcast language would strengthen Nigeria’s international presence and enable it to communicate its stories to a wider audience. Ndace, who was represented by the Director of General Services, Alhaji Danladi Abubakar, said the service would promote Nigeria’s culture, tourism, business opportunities and national image among Chinese-speaking audiences. He said the initiative followed agreements reached between Nigeria and China at the 2024 Forum on China-Africa Cooperation held in Beijing. According to him, VON also signed agreements with Xinhua News Agency and the Chinese Embassy in 2026 to promote content sharing, staff training, broadcasting capacity and media cooperation. In his remarks, the Executive Secretary of the Nigeria Press Council, Dili Ezughah, described the programme as an important step towards strengthening cultural diplomacy and people-to-people relations. He urged the partners to sustain the initiative, saying its success should be measured by its ability to promote mutual understanding and lasting relationships between citizens of both countries. item.title: Ododo flags off 38.5km Kogi road project
item.description: …Promises to End Decades of Poor Access By Soni Daniel, Northern Region Editor Kogi State Governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, on Thursday flagged off the construction of the 38.5-kilometre Kabba–Olle-Bunu–Iluke-Bunu Road in Kabba/Bunu Local Government Area, promising to address decades of poor road infrastructure in the area. The project, flagged off at Oke-Ofin, is expected to improve connectivity among communities in Bunu land, ease the movement of agricultural produce and expand access to economic opportunities. Speaking at the ceremony, Ododo described the project as the fulfilment of a long-standing aspiration of the people, assuring residents that his administration would not abandon any community, irrespective of its location. He said the road would mark a new chapter for the area by reconnecting communities that had remained isolated for years. The governor recalled how the deplorable condition of the road had affected farmers, businesses and residents, explaining that farmers struggled to transport their produce to markets, while indigenes living outside the state found it difficult to visit their ancestral homes. He disclosed that his personal experience during a visit to Iluke-Bunu following a security incident involving students had strengthened his resolve to rehabilitate the road. Ododo said the project was part of his administration’s commitment to complementing efforts to restore security with tangible development, stressing that peace without infrastructure and economic opportunities would remain incomplete. According to him, the road would facilitate the transportation of yams, cassava, cashew and other agricultural produce, reduce transportation costs, shorten travel time and stimulate commercial activities across Bunu land. The governor acknowledged the support of President Bola Tinubu, saying the increased financial resources available to state governments following the Federal Government’s economic reforms had helped subnational governments execute major infrastructure projects. He urged residents to embrace unity and take ownership of the project by monitoring its execution, protecting construction equipment and ensuring that quality standards were maintained. The Commissioner for Information and Communications, Kingsley Femi Fanwo, described the flag-off as a historic moment, citing his personal connection to Bunu land. Fanwo recalled trekking from Iluke to Ole-Bunu because of the poor condition of the road, which he said had remained in a deplorable state for more than 35 years. He said the project would open up several communities in Bunu to greater economic and social opportunities, adding that future generations would remember the intervention. The Commissioner for Education, an indigene of the benefiting community, also thanked the governor, describing the project as a major development for residents who had endured years of hardship because of the inaccessible road. item.title: 194 make first class as UNIZIK graduates 16,842
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Nnamdi Azikiwe University (UNIZIK), Awka, Anambra State, will graduate 16,842 students at its 20th and 21st combined convocation ceremonies scheduled for November 15 to 20, 2026, with 194 of the graduands earning First Class honours. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Ugochukwu Bond Anyaehie, disclosed this during a pre-convocation press briefing in Awka, where he also highlighted the institution’s academic, administrative, technological and infrastructural achievements. Anyaehie said the graduands comprised 14,803 first-degree recipients and 2,039 postgraduate students from the 2025 and 2026 academic sessions. A breakdown of the results showed that 4,230 students obtained Second Class Upper Division, while 7,992 graduated with Second Class Lower Division. Another 1,936 students obtained Third Class honours, while 65 graduated with Pass degrees. A further 486 earned unclassified medical and professional degrees. At the postgraduate level, 603 candidates obtained Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees, 29 earned Master of Philosophy/PhD degrees, 1,113 obtained Master’s degrees, while 294 graduated with Postgraduate Diplomas (PGDs). The Vice-Chancellor described the forthcoming convocation as an opportunity to celebrate the university’s growth and showcase achievements recorded under his administration’s vision of making a greater UNIZIK possible. He said the university had been ranked joint fourth among Nigerian universities in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings. He also disclosed that UNIZIK’s debate team won the 13th All Nigerian Universities Debate Championship (ANUDC), marking the first time the institution had clinched the title. Anyaehie recalled that the university’s athletes also won silver and bronze medals at the 12th Federation of African University Sports (FASU) Games held in Cairo, Egypt. On digital infrastructure, he said the university had been selected for the Federal Government’s $617.7 million Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) programme, supported by the Bank of Industry, Agence Française de Développement and the African Development Bank/Islamic Development Bank. He said the institution had expanded its internet bandwidth to 2Gbps through the Agence Française de Développement-Nigeria Research and Education Network (AFD-NgREN), adding that equipment supplied by Galaxy Backbone had been installed to activate an additional 300Mbps. The Vice-Chancellor further disclosed that his administration had established a TETFund ICT Experience Centre at Hall 2 of the university’s Digital Library to support training and research in artificial intelligence, robotics, cybersecurity and software engineering. He said the university had also upgraded its computer laboratories with 200 all-in-one desktop computers, 20 high-performance laptops, interactive smart screens, servers, enterprise network switches and video conferencing equipment. item.title: Oyo targets $3.4trn African market for artisans, creative businesses
item.description: By Adeola Badru Oyo State Government has unveiled plans to position local artisans, creative entrepreneurs and small businesses to tap into the estimated $3.4 trillion African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) market and expand their access to global export opportunities. The state government said it was determined to transform its rich cultural heritage into a commercially viable creative industry capable of generating wealth, creating employment and attracting foreign exchange through exports. Governor Seyi Makinde stated this at the Investment and Export Promotion for Art and Craft Businesses in Oyo State, tagged Oyo State Business Forum 2026: Where Oyo’s Makers Meet the World’s Buyers. The forum, held at the Ministry of Local Government Hall, Secretariat, Ibadan, was organised by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism in collaboration with the Oyo State Investment Promotion Agency (OYSIPA). Represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Musibau Babatunde, the governor said the initiative was a deliberate effort to reposition Oyo State as a major destination for creative enterprise and investment. Addressing government officials, investors, development partners, captains of industry and entrepreneurs, Makinde said the state was determined to ensure that locally produced goods gained international recognition and commercial value. “Today, we are not just gathered for another forum. We are gathered to make a declaration that Oyo State will no longer be known for its history, but for its entrepreneurial spirit. “We are gathered here around a common ambition to transform what our people create with their hands into products that the world recognises, values and buys,” he said. Tracing Oyo’s commercial heritage to the old Oyo Empire, Babatunde noted that the state had historically played an important role in regional commerce, with its people trading textiles, beads, ironworks and other products across West Africa long before the emergence of modern international trade. He said AfCFTA had presented another significant opportunity for the state to reclaim its position as a commercial powerhouse by expanding the reach of locally manufactured and processed products. According to him, the continental trade agreement is creating a single African market of approximately 1.4 billion people, with a combined economic output of about $3.4 trillion. He, however, challenged the state to move beyond recognising the opportunities offered by the agreement and take concrete steps to secure a significant share of its benefits. “The question before us is simple. Will Oyo State merely absorb this opportunity, or will we position ourselves to benefit from it? My answer is clear. Oyo State will be an active participant, and our artisans, creative entrepreneurs and small businesses will be among the driving forces of this ambition,” he said. item.title: ‘I’m Here’, Fubara Declares As Wike Inaugurates Rainbow Coalition, APC Campaign Council In Rivers
item.description: The Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, on Thursday, declared his unwavering support for the All Progressives Congress (APC), stating that he is fully involved in the Rainbow Coalition movement. He made the declaration as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, inaugurated members of the Rivers APC Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in the State. He urged members to demonstrate through their actions that they are committed to the political cause ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor said he expected members to be honest about their political convictions, stressing that those unwilling to support his position should openly take a different path rather than engage in double-dealing. He said his political decision is firm and would not be different whether expressed publicly or privately. “Don’t say you’re openly with me, and behind you’re doing a different thing. I’m here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day, in private and in secret. I have taken this position, and anybody who says he is not with me, gently go your way.” Gov. Fubara also urged members to put past political differences behind them, noting that the new campaign council has brought together a broader spectrum of political stakeholders, including some who were previously in opposition. He described the expanded composition of the council as an advantage that could strengthen the coalition’s chances if members worked together. Recalling the 2023 general elections, the governor said a similar political structure had helped secure victory for him and President Bola Tinubu, expressing confidence that the new council could deliver even more votes in 2027. He challenged members to approach the assignment with determination, insisting that electoral success would depend on their willingness to work collectively towards a common objective. “If we take it as a serious responsibility, a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisive, with a stronger vote that is more than what we did in 2023.” The governor congratulated members of the inaugurated council and assured those who were not included in the initial list that additional committees would be constituted and the structure could still be expanded. He expressed appreciation to the council’s leadership and other political stakeholders for their efforts, praying for success in the task ahead. The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, speaking while inaugurating members of the Rivers APC Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in Rivers State on Thursday, November 12, 2026. On his three million vote projection for President Bola Tinubu, Fubara said that nothing was impossible with dedication and seriousness. item.title: US Does Not ‘Need A Deal With Iran’, Says Trump
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said he was directing Vice President JD Vance to focus solely on domestic anti-fraud efforts and not negotiations with Tehran. “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. The development was after the US President defended the war against Iran Wednesday at a US Veterans Day commemoration that saw his defense secretary publicly admonished for a lack of decorum. “The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible,” Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington. “When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better place, more peaceful place, and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer.” U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP The war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes against Iran, has so far cost the lives of 23 US service members and wounded several hundred more, according to the latest Pentagon figures. Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which “has been waging war on America since 1979.” U.S. President Donald Trump and U.S. Vice President JD Vance participate in a wreath-laying ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2025 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP He stressed that US forces were acting to halt Iran’s capacity to build a nuclear weapon. Trump, 80, attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery’s Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a sacred symbol for America’s lost service members. item.title: UNIJOS Appoints First Female Vice Chancellor In 50-Year History
item.description: The University of Jos has appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the establishment of the institution. Her appointment was announced on Thursday by the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the University’s Governing Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent, during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council. Professor Lar takes over from Professor Tanko Ishaya, whose tenure as Vice Chancellor has come to an end. Presenting the letter of appointment to the incoming Vice Chancellor, Senator Bent charged her to remain focused in the discharge of her responsibilities as she prepares to lead the university. Her emergence marks a historic milestone for the University of Jos, as she becomes the first female Vice Chancellor in the institution’s history and the 11th substantive head of the university. item.title: Suspected Thugs Attack NDC Supporters In Lagos Ahead Of Peter Obi’s Town Hall
item.description: Suspected political thugs on Thursday, November 12, 2026, attacked members and supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Oregun area of Ikeja, Lagos State, disrupting preparations for a town hall meeting scheduled to be addressed by the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. The incident, which occurred around 11:00 a.m. at the Classique Event Centre along Kudirat Abiola Way, sent scores of attendees scampering for safety and triggered panic in the surrounding commercial district. Motorists plying Kudirat Abiola Way were forced to make abrupt U-turns to avoid the melee, while pedestrians fled the area. Crowd of NDC supporters gather outside town hall after attack by thugs. According to witnesses at the scene, neither Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, nor Kwankwaso, a former governor of Kano State, had arrived at the venue when the attackers struck. Shattered glass on the floor, as captured by our reporter at the scene of the disrupted town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Oregun, Lagos State, on Thursday, November 12, 2026 : Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels TV https://t.co/lR2QKFNf8v — Channels Television (@channelstv) November 12, 2026 Shattered glass littered the floor of the disrupted venue, while several vehicles belonging to NDC members and supporters stood vandalised within the premises. One party supporter, speaking to Channels Television after sustaining a head injury, alleged that hoodlums armed with cutlasses invaded the area in an attempt to derail the gathering. He noted that additional NDC members were mobilised to resist the assailants, eventually forcing them to retreat. “When I arrived out here, we reacted to our president without fear. They started fighting back, breaking our vehicles, and destroying property,” the injured supporter told Channels Television, adding that attendees retaliated in self-defence despite being outnumbered and warning of heightened tensions ahead of the 2027 elections. ﻿ Armed policemen and security patrol vehicles were subsequently deployed to the Classique Event Centre to restore order and prevent further escalation. Following the arrival of law enforcement, the atmosphere gradually stabilised, with NDC supporters seen dancing, singing, and defiantly raising the party’s flag as they awaited the arrival of their presidential ticket. The NDC governorship candidate in Lagos State, Funso Doherty, also arrived at the venue to assess the extent of the damage. A supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is seen raising the party’s flag at the venue of the party’s town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos State on Thursday, November 12, 2026. (Photo: Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels TV) As of the time of filing this report, the exact circumstances behind the attack and the identities of the perpetrators remained unclear, with the Lagos State Police Command yet to release an official statement. item.title: Five key allies of Peter Obi who parted ways with him after 2023
item.description: ‎ The recent decision by Yunusa Tanko a leading figure in the Obidient Movement, to accept an appointment as Director-General of the presidential campaign council of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) candidate has once again drawn attention to the growing list of notable political associates who have distanced themselves from former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi. ‎ ‎Since the conclusion of the 2023 presidential election, Obi has remained one of the country’s most influential opposition politicians. ‎However, several key figures who played important roles in his campaign, political structure, or movement have either left the Labour Party, aligned with other political interests, or openly criticized his political direction. Obi is presently the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 election. ‎ ‎These defections have triggered renewed debate about the cohesion of the political movement that emerged around Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign. 2027: IGP warns officers against compromise Thugs attack Pantami’s campaign rally in Gombe ‎ ‎While Obi continues to command a loyal support base across the country, the departure of several high-profile associates underscores the challenge of maintaining political unity and building a durable structure ahead of the next electoral cycle. ‎ However, his present alliance with Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, the leader of Kwankwasiyya Movement, is seen by many as a plus to him. ‎ ‎Below are five of such most prominent names. ‎ ‎ YUNUSA TANKO tanko yunusa ‎ ‎Perhaps the latest and most symbolic departure is that of Yunusa Tanko, who served as National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement and was one of the most visible defenders of Obi after the 2023 election. ‎ ‎Tanko was a key mobiliser of Obi’s support base across the country and regularly represented the movement on national television and at political events. However, he recently accepted an appointment as Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council of SDP presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, effectively moving away from Obi’s political camp. ‎ ‎YUSUF DATTI BABA-AHMED ‎ ‎As Obi’s running mate in the 2023 election, Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed was one of the central figures of the Labour Party ticket. ‎Although he has not openly defected to another political camp in the manner of some of Obi’s former associates, reports indicate that he publicly expressed disagreements with aspects of Obi’s political direction, fueling speculation about differences within the former presidential ticket. ‎ ‎KENNETH OKONKWO ‎ ‎Actor, lawyer and politician, Kenneth Okonkwo was one of the most vocal spokespersons of the Obi campaign during the 2023 presidential race. ‎ ‎In July 2024, he announced his exit from the Labour Party and openly criticized Obi’s handling of the party’s leadership crisis.
